name: Schneider Electric Infrastructure Ltd
title: Schneider Electric Infrastructure Ltd - 534139 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Schneider Electric Infrastructure Q4 FY26 sales were flat at INR590 crore as customers deferred dispatches; FY26 orders grew 27.4% and backlog rose about 50%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 sales were roughly flat YoY at INR590 crore, with management attributing the shortfall to customers, mainly EPC contractors, asking to hold dispatches amid geopolitical disruption. Q4 profit margin fell to about 6%, with management citing roughly 2.5 percentage points of commodity impact from copper and aluminium up over 30% and steel up about 10% in FY26. Full-year FY26 orders grew 27.4%, sales 9.6% and profit before tax 10.1%, with backlog up about 50%. Q4 order intake was deliberately selective because customers resisted variable price clauses. Management gave no quantified guidance and declined to size data centre, BESS or market-share opportunities.

segments.name: Data centres
segments.commentary: Management said data centres are about 10% to 12% of the current order backlog and expected to rise; no quantified opportunity was given because hyperscaler designs differ.

segments.name: Energy storage (BESS)
segments.commentary: Company does not make batteries; it offers the rest of the system (AC/DC equipment, switchgear, structures, software) with battery sourced from partners. No addressable market figure given.

segments.name: Services and modernisation
segments.commentary: Services rose to about 15% of revenue per analyst framing; management said modernisation and retrofit margins are falling under L1-based competition.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the delayed Q4 deliveries to recover in Q1 FY27, conditional on LPG and copper supply issues easing.
Management says commodity margin pressure is largely a one-off and that margins should improve with mix and efficiency, but gave no quantified target.
Management said the Q4 margin dip is largely phasing of overheads and that costs will catch up over the full year.
Management gave no numerical guidance on order growth, revenue or margins for FY27.
capex_capacity: Depreciation rose in Q4 as capex approved earlier began capitalising at Q4 end; no capacity or utilisation figures given.
Company plans a Baroda manufacturing line for dry-type Trihal transformers (33 kV class, E4/C4F1 endurance rating, seismic compliance), targeting data centres, metros and commercial buildings.
Management said the company is setting up a skill centre in North India for PFC training of DISCOM staff.
Management said the company is exploring exports, including for data centre products; no order details given.
demand_pricing: Q4 order intake was low because the company was selective, booking only orders with variable price clauses that allow commodity pass-through; customers were reluctant to accept these.
Management said deliveries of roughly 10% to 12% of Q4 orders were deferred to the next quarter, but declined to give a precise quantum.
Commodity hedging covers 50% to 60% of exposure; forex is hedged via order-by-order PO hedges and a net ARAP hedge.
Large projects above six months are contracted with price-variation clauses to pass commodity increases to customers.
Demand drivers cited: non-fossil capacity about 280 GW against a 500 GW target, data centre pipeline about 3 GW signed for 1.5 to 2 years, and government capex up about 11.5% to INR12.2 lakh crore.
Management said the company is not cost leader in BESS and competes on quality and advisory software.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 revenue shortfall and whether it recovers?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers, mainly EPC contractors with end-customer dependency, asked to hold dispatches; management hopes for recovery in Q1 FY27 once LPG and copper issues ease.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 gross margin decline and when does margin recovery come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 2.5 percentage points of Q4 margin hit to commodities and said the margin mix shifted toward lower-margin modernisation and projects, but gave no recovery timeline.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the data centre opportunity and its share of backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres are about 10% to 12% of backlog and should rise; no quantified opportunity was given as designs vary by hyperscaler.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS scope and competitiveness?
qa_highlights.answer: Company supplies the system excluding batteries, with structures and switchgear mostly made in India; management said it is not a cost leader and competes on quality and software.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 order intake weak and sales growth in single digits for most of FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was selective on orders because customers would not accept variable pricing; sales depend on customer dispatch clearance and credit, so deliveries are held where cash is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging and capital allocation framework?
qa_highlights.answer: Commodity hedging covers 50% to 60%; forex is hedged on PO and net ARAP basis. No dividend or liquidity framework was detailed.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (copper and aluminium up over 30%, steel up about 10%) and the pass-through lag on fixed-price contracts.
Customer dispatch deferrals and credit delays, particularly for EPC-channel customers; cash conversion risk.
Margin trend: gross margin fell about 160 bps in FY26 and mix is shifting toward lower-margin modernisation work.
Order intake momentum in Q1 FY27 after weak Q4 bookings, and whether the roughly 10% to 12% of Q4 deferred deliveries are recognised.
Competitive intensity in BESS and in L1-driven renewable and brownfield tenders.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on long-term India demand but defensive and evasive on near-term numbers: it declined to quantify data centre, BESS and market-share opportunities and deferred delivery quantum, attributing the weak quarter to geopolitics and customer timing.
key_quotes: And that's why if you look at the order overall, the backlog which is there is around 50% up from the last year.
We are absolutely and equally sensitive about profitability. So we are not chasing. We are selective in certain areas.
We do not make batteries, okay?
Sir, not a very straightforward answer because we will not be -- because there are various, as I think Omkar was mentioning about it.
